seasons.metaDescription: A cozy living room cinema in Vienna showing carefully curated films about friendship, community, and belonging. Join us every Wednesday at 19h30 for Season 1: SHARING.
seasons.blurb: This first season of movie-seeing brings a collectively curated series of films, first watched with friends who are away or ever popping up in conversations with those in Vienna. The stories too speak about friendship, about a sense of community, of belonging. Of being present and witnessing the world.

program.title: The Fire Within: A Requiem for Katja and Maurice Krafft
Snacks: a selection of salty shorts

seasons.blurb: In this season we will explore the ways we connect and disconnect with each another. On tangled webs of people and emotions, flirting is all around — from Claire’s very particular knee to soviet Ninotchka falling hard for the charms of capitalism. What’s in a brief exchange of looks? Is flirting just innocent play? Or can the aftermath haunt us?

program.title: Brief Encounters: a selection of shorts

shorts.title: All the Boys are Called Patrick

seasons.blurb: We dive into Summer with stories that speak of aquatic adventures and underwater worlds. Whether it is the sea or human psyche, we explore what lies beneath the surface: are these unseen worlds full of wonder, or are there dark truths waiting to be unveiled?

program.title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou

seasons.blurb: August in the city? We'll be by the seaside. Swimming in salty waters, in true silly season spirit with Jacques Tati, moving to end-of-Summer blues with Éric Rohmer's A Summer's Tale.

After Summer, September is a return. To home, to the routines, to ourselves. Maybe a new beginning. Or an ending - after all, the leaves on the trees are yellowing and falling... So this season we'll be seeing stories of Returning: to a home taken from us (The Time that Remains, Return to Seoul), to a community that once welcomed us, to dreaming places (La Chimera)... Or we can find a point of no return (Happy Together). Glad to be back.

hello schön.kinoers! 🎃 here is the program for this month. in full halloween spirit, October is MADDENING: along these four weeks, the level of terror will rise from daily life psychosis in Red Desert to full blown-up psychological terror in Possession. 👻 no ghosts or zombies here, just the sheer terror of real life… 🙂🙂🙂🙂🙂🙂🙂🙂🙂🙂

It's the season of harvest and reflection: when we gather what remains, notice what has been lost, and prepare for what will return. We look at what was overlooked and say "there is still beauty here". This is a cinema of gleaning: of gathering fragments of life, grace, and feeling before the year exhales.

It's not nice to eat your friends…! Try telling that to a bear. Grizzly Man is a tragicomedy documentary of Timothy Treadwell, an untrained film-maker who believed had a special connection to bears in Alaska. Until one day he is eaten by one. Herzog takes hundreds of hours of videotape and assembles them into a story: sublime, dramatic shots of the bears, teaching us about nature and… well… human stupidity. In line with current world news, here's to a bizarre start of the year!

Some call it a masterpiece, others say it’s the worst they’ve ever seen. João de Deus (João of God) is everything but a holy man. As a matter of fact, he is utterly disgusting: a perverted intellectual, passionate about Schubert, cinema, and… the landlord’s daughter. This can only go downhill from here. Like last month’s Timothy Treadwell, João is an outcast from society. The film follows him, witness to a series of absurd encounters in a Lisbon that no longer exists. A comedy of the absurd, a really boring movie, or simply bad? I guess we’ll find out. In true Lisbon spirit, better watched (or rather washed down?) with beer.
